title: SMB: Multiple requests in same packet fixed
description:
o When there are multiple requests in the same packet only the last
  appeared in the Packet List. NOTE: These are not AndX'd requests.
o Added FID and subcommand on each SMB header in the Packet Detail.
o Limited pathname length in the Packet List to 40 chars in order
  to make multiple command names more noticible.
o In some request types the FID was not displayed.

notes.body: (Is this the universe's way of saying that the packet list pane should be a tree rather than a list, with multiple summaries under a top-level summary?)

As an analyst of 40 years and having looked at thousands of captures, I can tell you that a well-thought-out summary saves hours of work. In this case, it is very easy to miss the fact that a frame contains multiple requests. The summary is just that, a summary of the most important information about a given packet.
Is there a change in the code that you require to merge this request?
No.

How does this work when packets are dissected in random order, such as when scrolling upwards and or going to random packets in Wireshark? Or rather, is it possible for the same packet number to be dissected twice for different reasons, by different `epan_dissect_t`? I think possibly.

In which case you might (if doing this approach) need to use `register_frame_end_routine` to set last_fnum back to zero at the end of a frame.

There are other approaches, involving using packet scoped proto data (or helper functions around it), or the current layer number for the protocol.

There isn't an issue with these multi-command requests during random
selection or scrolling because all of the dissection and handling is
performed within a single frame.

Does this address your other comment as well?

No, because last_fnum is not reset between packets. If, for example, you click on a SMB packet with one request in the packet list, then multiselect (or unselect), then click on the same packet again, then "last_num" will be equal to pinfo->num when starting to dissect the single request in the packet, and "mult_cmds" will be set to true, even though there aren't multiple commands in the packet.

To make that create a problem, you have to make it affect the columns. Here's an example:

Open [myandx.pcapng](/uploads/e471f68ba0378bc5e54d9a2e3539ff73/myandx.pcapng) and filter for smb. Click on the first SMB packet, packet 4, so it displays in the Packet Details (this sets last_num to 4):

![image](/uploads/bb6a1df095f99d8227f1845ec89c24d7/image.png)

Now click on the icon in the toolbar to enable/disable coloring rules, which causes a redissection and the column cache to be cleared:

![image](/uploads/e5884e55af1bdfae7be93285a306cc07/image.png)

Note that the Info column for packet 4 **changed** because the packet was the first dissected to redo the columns and colors, and it was dissected with `last_num == 4` because `last_num` was set by clicking on the packet to dissect it for the packet details.
The Info column in the second picture is what happens if frame 4 is dissected with `mult_cmds == true` for the first (and only) message in frame 4; it doesn't clear the Info column from NBT.
Hmm, we can try, but if those are static variables, and not stored with each packet, I think that they might still have problems with random packet access.
Okay. Before I submit this, I'll test random packet access within a large capture containing multiple commands. (I have many.)
I tested it using very random access in a large capture, and it worked fine. I'll submit this tomorrow after some additional testing.

The "Session message" text, which happens on the first SMB frame, is a problem I haven't been able to solve. Wouldn't register_frame_end_routine() make the global variable zero between iterations, rendering mult_cmds useless?

It would only make the global variable zero at the end of the entire frame, but it wouldn't do it between iterations of SMB messages in the same frame, so I think that's exactly what you'd want. It doesn't get called at the end of dissect_smb(), it gets called at the end of dissect_frame().
It looks like this introduced #20614. Can you take a look?
I didn't change this code. It's been there for years. There doesn't seem to be anything wrong with it. How does it look to you?

This line introduced #20810, since offset has already been advanced beyond the file name in the packet due to the `COUNT_BYTES(fn_len);` call after the file name was added to the tree before in this function.

I'm not sure what's intended here though. Is it adding a new item to the si->smbtree, or appending text to si->smbtree?  
First one is implemented (`proto_tree_add_string`), but the second is mostly used (`proto_item_append_text`).

Hi, the proto_tree_add_string() is not supposed to be there. I'll create a
new MR for that. As a side note, this is not the current code that was
merged in #21414. I have many test captures with multiple commands in
the same frame, but none have Create File calls (only Create_AndX calls).
